input.command: git ls-files; cat package.json index.js README.md; ls test* 2>/dev/null; cat test/* 2>/dev/null | head -50

result.builder:
Make one pull request for https://github.com/o/strutil/issues/7 that meets every one of these acceptance lines:
- index.js exports padLeft(s, width, fill), which pads s on the left with fill (a space when fill is not given) to width characters
- padLeft returns s unchanged when s is already width characters or longer
- README.md has a section for every function index.js exports
- npm test passes

Steps:
1. Read index.js, README.md, package.json and test/strutil.test.js. The package is an ES module ("type": "module"); index.js currently exports capitalize, slugify and truncate. `npm test` runs `node --test`.
2. In index.js add and export `padLeft(s, width, fill = ' ')` with a short doc comment in the style of the existing functions. It returns `s` unchanged when `s.length >= width`; otherwise it adds `fill` on the left until the result is exactly `width` characters (e.g. padLeft('42', 5, '0') === '00042', padLeft('ab', 4) === '  ab'). `s.padStart(width, fill)` meets this for a one-character fill. Do not change the existing functions.
3. In README.md make sure there is a section for EVERY function index.js exports, not only the new one. Note that README.md today has sections for capitalize and truncate but NONE for slugify, so add a `## slugify(s)` section (describe it: lower case, runs of non-alphanumerics become single dashes, leading/trailing dashes removed) as well as a `## padLeft(s, width, fill)` section (pads on the left with fill, default a space, to width characters; returns s unchanged when already width or longer; mention the 42 -> 00042 example). Use the same `## name(args)` heading style as the existing sections and keep them before the `## Tests` section.
4. In test/strutil.test.js import padLeft and add tests: padLeft('42', 5, '0') === '00042'; padLeft('ab', 4) === '  ab' (default space); padLeft('abcde', 5, '0') === 'abcde' and padLeft('abcdef', 3) === 'abcdef' (unchanged when already width or longer).
5. Run `npm test` and confirm it exits 0 with all tests passing. Also check that every name in `node -e "import('./index.js').then(m=>console.log(Object.keys(m)))"` has a matching heading in README.md.
6. Commit and open the pull request referencing issue #7.
result.verifier:
Check out the pull request head and run every check below from the repository root. There is one check per acceptance line of https://github.com/o/strutil/issues/7, in the same order. Report PASS or FAIL for each with the command output that decided it.

Check 1 — "index.js exports padLeft(s, width, fill), which pads s on the left with fill (a space when fill is not given) to width characters"
Run: node --input-type=module -e "import * as m from './index.js'; console.log(typeof m.padLeft); console.log(JSON.stringify([m.padLeft('42',5,'0'), m.padLeft('ab',4), m.padLeft('7',3,'*'), m.padLeft('',2,'x')]))"
PASS: first line is `function` and the array is ["00042","  ab","**7","xx"] (padding added on the left with the given fill, a space when fill is omitted, result exactly width characters long).
FAIL: padLeft is not exported, throws, pads on the right, uses a different default than a space, or any result is not width characters long.

Check 2 — "padLeft returns s unchanged when s is already width characters or longer"
Run: node --input-type=module -e "import {padLeft} from './index.js'; console.log(JSON.stringify([padLeft('abcde',5,'0'), padLeft('abcdef',3), padLeft('abcdef',3,'0')]))"
PASS: output is ["abcde","abcdef","abcdef"].
FAIL: any value differs from its input s (padded, truncated or otherwise changed), or the call throws.

Check 3 — "README.md has a section for every function index.js exports"
Run: node --input-type=module -e "import * as m from './index.js'; console.log(Object.keys(m).filter(k=>typeof m[k]==='function').join(' '))" to list exported functions, then read README.md (e.g. `grep -n '^#' README.md`) and look for a section for each listed name.
PASS: every exported function (expected at least capitalize, slugify, truncate, padLeft) has its own section in README.md, i.e. a heading that names that function, with text describing it.
FAIL: any exported function has no section in README.md. Note: before this change README.md had no slugify section, so check slugify specifically.

Check 4 — "npm test passes"
Run: npm test
PASS: the test run reports all tests passing (no failures).
FAIL: any test fails or the run errors.

Advisory (not pass/fail conditions):
- Expect `npm test` to exit with status 0 and to include tests for padLeft (default fill and the unchanged case).
- Existing functions capitalize, slugify and truncate should behave as before.
- README section headings would ideally follow the existing `## name(args)` style and appear before `## Tests`.

text:
I wrote both briefs for issue #7 (add `padLeft()` to strutil) and the harness accepted them. I changed nothing in the repository.

The main thing I found: `README.md` has no section for `slugify` today, even though `index.js` already exports it. So the line "README.md has a section for every function index.js exports" means writing more than the `padLeft` docs. A pull request that only documents `padLeft` would fail that line.

**Builder brief:**
- Add and export `padLeft(s, width, fill = ' ')` in `index.js`. It returns `s` unchanged when `s` is already `width` or longer.
- Add README sections for both `padLeft` and `slugify`, in the existing `## name(args)` heading style.
- Add tests to `test/strutil.test.js`: zero padding (42 → 00042), the default space fill, and the unchanged case.
- Run `npm test`, then check that every exported function has a matching README heading.

**Verifier brief:** one check per acceptance line, in order:
1. A `node` script imports `index.js`, confirms `padLeft` is a function, and checks it pads on the left with the given fill, or a space when none is given, to exactly `width` characters.
2. A `node` script confirms `padLeft` returns `s` unchanged when `s` is already `width` characters or longer.
3. List the exported functions and confirm each has its own section in `README.md`, checking `slugify` by name.
4. `npm test` reports no failing tests.

Stricter points that the acceptance lines don't require sit under an Advisory heading, not in the pass/fail conditions. These are: exit status 0, tests covering `padLeft`, the existing functions behaving as before, and the heading style.
